excluded_images.reason: Cover-page hero image showing a multi-instrument tabletop arrangement, not a single product. Excluded from per-product scoring; retained as an optional 'multi-object scene' stress-test case (see note below) rather than a standard catalogue entry.
excluded_images.optional_reference_caption: A wide arrangement of stainless-steel surgical instruments including scalpels, scissors, forceps, and clamps laid out on a blue sterile drape under an operating-room light.

notes_for_benchmark_harness: Each image has 3 reference_captions (not 1) — use all 3 as references for corpus-level BLEU/CIDEr/ROUGE-L scoring, which is standard practice and more robust than single-reference scoring.

key_specs is intentionally free-form/heterogeneous across categories (diagnostic devices vs. surgical sets have different relevant fields) — do not force a single fixed key set across all products when scoring attribute extraction; instead compute per-image field-level P/R/F1 against each image's own key_specs keys, then macro-average.
certifications and intended_setting are list-valued fields — score with set-based precision/recall (e.g. Jaccard or exact-set-match), not string exact-match.

price_eur/price_unit are structured numeric/categorical fields, not caption content — do not include price expectations in caption-quality scoring, only in attribute-extraction scoring, since VLMs cannot reliably read tiny catalogue price tags from the product photo alone; treat 'price correctly extracted' as an optional/bonus field rather than a required one, or drop it from attribute scoring entirely unless the price is visibly printed on the product packaging in the image itself (it is not, in these images).

MC-HERO-COLLAGE.jpg is deliberately excluded from the main 6-item scoring set because it depicts multiple products at once and has no single ground-truth product_code/key_specs — including it in the main pool would corrupt attribute-extraction metrics. Use it only as an optional qualitative multi-object captioning example if desired.
